free_tier.stated: No free tier. The WireGuard tunnel is "2 [EUR] per month" at the campaign rate (list "5 [EUR]"), with "Included transit 1 TB free".

egress.terms: "Included transit 1 TB free", then "Additional transit 0.35 [EUR]/TB" at the campaign rate (list 0.50). Capacity is "up to 1 Gbit/s".; ingress: tcp+udp
egress.free_allowance: "Included transit 1 TB free", then "Additional transit 0.35 [EUR]/TB" at the campaign rate (list 0.50). Capacity is "up to 1 Gbit/s".

interface_detail: Order and manage in the panel; no API named on the pages read.
chaining: A tunnel plus one routed IPv4 on a free-tier VM is the whole stack; the same tunnel can carry a /29 if more addresses are bought at 0.70 each.

limits.value: 1 TB per month included, then EUR 0.35 per TB
account verification before the tunnel comes online

binding_note: The 1 TB allowance is metered and priced, not capped, so a 1 TiB month costs about EUR 0.04 beyond the included terabyte and nothing stops it. 1 TiB is about 10 percent more than 1 TB, so the decimal allowance runs out slightly before a binary terabyte.

identity_cost.detail: Registration is an email plus a 6-digit mail code, but the service is gated on payment and on a verified account: "Once your account is verified, getting your tunnel online is sssssimple." The privacy page names what is collected: "Identite et contact : prenom, nom, email, telephone", and Stripe is the payment processor.

reliability_note: Mitigated attack traffic is not counted against the allowance, which matters if the address is ever a target.
confidence_note: Price, allowance, overage rate, IP price and tunnel types are all first-party. What a verified account requires beyond email and card is unread.

evidence.proved: WireGuard tunnel 2 EUR/month (list 5), 1 TB transit included, additional transit 0.35 EUR/TB, additional IPv4 0.70 EUR/IP, term discounts up to 15 percent
the tunnel carries routed IPv4 or IPv6 and survives a changing client address without dynamic DNS
"IPv4 addresses from 0.70 [EUR]/IP"; DDoS mitigation included up to 7 Tb/s and mitigated traffic is not counted
name, email and phone are collected at signup; Stripe is the payment processor

price_per_tb_month: EUR 2 per month for a WireGuard tunnel, EUR 0.70 per additional IPv4, EUR 0.35 per TB above the first TB
notes: Cheapest per TiB with a real included terabyte: EUR 0.35 per extra TB is about USD 0.40 per TiB at the campaign rate, and mitigated DDoS traffic is excluded from the count. The price is a campaign price with a struck-through list price, so it can end. Registration collects a phone number even though the form marks optional fields as optional.

extras.wg_detail: The tunnel is ordered in the panel and configured on the client's side: "Each endpoint has a public and private key", and the product page describes routed delivery: "It keeps configuration readable, establishes sessions quickly, and carries routed IPv4 or IPv6 traffic". IPv4 is a separate line item at "0.70 [EUR]/IP".
extras.volume_stated: "Included transit 1 TB free", then "Additional transit 0.35 [EUR]/TB" at the campaign rate (list 0.50). Capacity is "up to 1 Gbit/s".
extras.transit_note: The vendor routes the prefix to the tunnel from its own network and reports 1 to 7 ms routes.
